next_step: Finalize POC SOW and pricing for Dedicated 3-node pool
notes:
Account background: LumenQuery is a mid-market SaaS provider of knowledge search and insights for customer support teams. Product team (CTO + Head of Search) wants to add semantic search and unified embeddings across product docs, support logs, and KB.

Recent history / timeline (concise):
- 2025-01-15: Intro call (Aisha) — qualifying: team size, high-level use case, interest in hosted first for POC.
- 2025-01-20: Technical deep-dive with SE (Marco) — shared benchmark expectations and sample corpus. (see ff-20250120-5d3a)
- 2025-01-27: Sent pricing deck + security FAQ. Finance asked for Dedicated pricing band.
- 2025-01-30: Follow-up call re: vector DB choices and batch ingestion (see ff-20250130-a9b2).
- 2025-02-04: Legal raised residency question; wants confirmation of control-plane data flow for Dedicated.

Use-case & requirements — notes from SE & product: 
- Primary workload: embeddings for semantic search + periodic re-indexing (nightly batch jobs).
- Corpus: ~2M documents initially, grows to ~12M over 12 months.
- Batch requirements: large nightly vectorization job (target ~4-6M vectors per night in peak months); prefer incremental delta processing.
- Online requirements: query-side semantic search: target p95 query latency <= 250ms for top-k retrieval on 99th-percentile index shards.
- Embedding throughput target for production (after Dedicated): steady-state 1500 vectors/sec for bulk ingestion, burst to 5k vectors/sec during backfill windows.
- Storage/DB: currently evaluating pgvector + Postgres for prototyping; considering Pinecone/Weaviate for production. Need Redwood compatibility with both simple vector ingestion and direct blob storage to S3 for long-term cold vectors.
- Routing/fallback: want Hosted API for quick POC, but Dedicated preferred for production due to residency and throughput SLAs. Also need automatic fallback to smaller model variant under load spikes.

Security & compliance notes: 
- Must support SSO (SAML) and enterprise audit logs.
- Data residency: customer requires EU residency for customer-facing docs (some customers in EU). For production, they want VPC private deployment or Dedicated in eu-west region.
- KMS integration required for encryption-at-rest of vectors/keys.

POC scope (proposed):
- 2-week POC using Hosted API to embed a 100k-sample of documents + integrate with pgvector demo cluster. Measure embedding latency, token costs, and end-to-end search P95.
- Success criteria: indexing throughput (>=1.2k vectors/sec sustained for batch), query p95 <= 250ms on 1M sample index, embedding quality on 10 curated evaluation queries (>= baseline similarity score).
- Post-POC: price Dedicated 3-node pool (reserved) to support 1500 v/s ingestion, 99th p95 SLA and VPC peering.

Commercial / Pricing conversations:
- Interested in committed Dedicated discount tiers if ARR/yield matches $75k-$150k guidance.
- Wants clear breakdown of Hosted per-embedding unit costs vs Dedicated unit economics.

Direct quotes & friction: 
- "We need predictable cost when the monthly vector count jumps — can't have surprise bills from embeddings spikes." (CTO)
- Legal: "Confirm where model telemetry and prompt traces are stored for Hosted POC."

Open links / artifacts: pricing_deck_2025.pptx, POC_SOW_v1.pdf, security_faq_responses.docx (Drive). Gmail thread thread-1689342 contains CFO questions on committed spend.

Next steps (short):
- Team to sign POC SOW by 2025-02-10.
- SE to provision test Hosted API keys + sample ingestion pipeline (Marco).
- Legal follow-up: provide data-flow diagram and residency note (Aisha).

Notes on blockers: budget needs sign-off from CFO, legal needs explicit residency statement, and vector DB ingestion performance on their chosen stack (pgvector) is unproven at scale.
activity_summary: POC planned: hosted API to validate embeddings + pgvector prototype. If pass, convert to Dedicated reserved pool. Main technical risk: integration throughput + residency/legal sign-off. Pricing negotiation pending after POC results.
